title: Egg omelet with meat and dark‑green vegetables

content.title: About
content.content: An omelet made from eggs, enriched with meat (such as ham or chicken breast) and dark‑green vegetables (spinach, broccoli, kale). Additional fat (oil or cream) is added to enhance flavor and energy density.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Eggs are one of the oldest foods used by humans.
Dark‑green vegetables get their color from chlorophyll, which also contributes a distinctive taste.
Meat in the omelet boosts iron and vitamin B12, essential for blood formation.
A small amount of added fat improves absorption of fat‑soluble vitamins (A, D, E, K).
The omelet can be easily customized by changing the type of meat and vegetables.

items.title: Rich in high‑quality protein
items.content: Eggs and meat provide complete proteins needed for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Source of B‑vitamins
items.content: B2, B6 and B12 support energy metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: High in iron
items.content: Meat and dark‑green vegetables supply easily absorbable iron important for hemoglobin.

items.title: Antioxidant properties
items.content: Spinach and broccoli contain lutein, zeaxanthin and vitamin C, protecting cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Heart‑friendly fats
items.content: Monounsaturated and polyunsaturated fats from added oil help maintain healthy cholesterol levels.

items.title: Egg allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to egg white proteins.

items.title: Cholesterol content
items.content: Egg yolks contain cholesterol; people with hypercholesterolemia should monitor portion size.

items.title: Sodium in processed meat
items.content: Cured meats (ham, bacon) can be high in salt, which is a concern for hypertension.

items.title: Foodborne illness risk
items.content: Undercooked eggs or meat may harbor pathogens such as Salmonella or Campylobacter.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the omelet hot, optionally garnish with fresh herbs, and add a yogurt‑based or tomato sauce. It works well as a standalone dish or as a filling for wraps.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the cooked omelet in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 2 days. Reheat in a pan or microwave, adding a little oil to prevent drying out.
